label: 2.R Exam Practice 2: Error Detection and Encryption

steps.label: Do Now: Parity (1 of 3)
steps.content:
Do Now: Parity (1 of 3)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does the receiver check each byte when it arrives, and not the sender before it leaves?Show the answer

Errors happen on the way. Only the receiver sees what actually arrived.

From 2.2. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2021, Question 6(a). Four 7-bit binary values are transmitted from one computer to another. A parity bit is added to each binary value creating 8-bit binary values. All the binary values are transmitted and received correctly. Identify whether each 8-bit binary value has been sent using odd or even parity.

Total: 4 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: odd or even parity

steps.text: A similar question. These bytes were received correctly. Was each one sent with odd or even parity?
steps.visual:
11000110
10110000

steps.text: Received correctly means nothing changed on the way. So the count of 1s still fits the parity that was used.
steps.visual: count the 1s, then match the count to a parity type

steps.text: Count the 1s in the whole byte. The parity bit counts too.
steps.visual:
11000110
1, 2, 3, 4

steps.text: 4 is an even number. So this byte fits the parity type named after even numbers.
steps.visual: 11000110 → 4 ones

steps.text: The second byte: count the 1s again.
steps.visual: 10110000 → 3 ones

steps.text: 3 is an odd number. So this byte fits the other parity type. Now count the 1s in each byte on your slide.
steps.visual: count, then decide: is the count odd or even?

steps.label: Do Now: Parity (2 of 3)
steps.content:
Do Now: Parity (2 of 3)

Think → Pair → ShareA parity check is quick and simple. Why do networks still use other checks as well?Show the answer

No single check finds every error. Using more than one check means fewer errors get through.

From 2.2. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2021, Question 6(b). The 8-bit binary value 10110001 is transmitted and received as 10110010. A parity check does not identify any errors in the binary value received.

Total: 1 mark

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: a change the check misses

steps.text: A similar case. This byte is sent, and a different byte arrives. The parity check finds no error.
steps.visual:
Sent: 11000010
Received: 10100010

steps.text: First find the bits that changed. Bit 2 and bit 3 are different.
steps.visual:
Sent: 11000010
Received: 10100010

steps.text: Look closely: bit 2 was 1 and became 0. Bit 3 was 0 and became 1.
Now count the 1s in each byte, as the receiver does.
steps.visual:
Sent: 11000010 → 3
Received: 10100010 → 3

steps.text: A parity check only counts the 1s. It does not look at where each 1 is.
Your question: do the same with 10110001 and 10110010. Find the bits that changed, count the 1s, and write what you see as your reason.

steps.label: Do Now: Encryption (3 of 3)
steps.content:
Do Now: Encryption (3 of 3)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy do exam questions on encryption reward exact terms, like the ones in the syllabus?Show the answer

An exact term shows the examiner you know the idea. A vague word could mean many things.

From 2.3. Part (a): Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2026, Question 2(e)(i). Part (b): Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2026, Question 4(c)(ii). Part (c): Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2022, Question 7(d).

Total: 4 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: types and terms

steps.text: A similar question. Give two types of parity check.
Ask: how are the types different? With one, the count of 1s must come out odd. With the other, it must come out even.
steps.visual:
count must be odd
count must be even

steps.text: Name each type after its difference: odd parity and even parity.
steps.visual:
odd parity
even parity

steps.text: Your part (a): how are the types of encryption different? One uses a single key that both people share. The other uses two different keys. Write the name of each type.
steps.visual:
one shared key: ?
two different keys: ?

steps.text: A similar question. State what is meant by a parity bit. Say what it is, then what it is used for.
steps.visual:
What is it? an extra bit
What is it for? making the count of 1s odd or even

steps.text: Your part (b): do the same for a key. What is it made of? Which job does it do in the process?
steps.visual: what it is + what it is for

steps.text: Your part (c): Eve intercepts the data on the way. She does not have the key. What does the data look like to her?

steps.label: Error Detection and Encryption Exam Practice
steps.content:
Topic 2 Review: Exam Practice 2

Error Detection and Encryption

Year 10

  • Today: real exam questions on error detection and encryption.
  • Also: be the sender and the receiver in ARQ, and fix answers that lose marks.
Think → Pair → ShareA question has 5 marks. Why plan five different points before you write?Show the answer

Each mark is for a different point. A plan shows whether you have enough different points, so you do not repeat one.

steps.label: Error Detection: The Odd Parity Check
steps.content:
Error Detection: The Odd Parity Check

Think → Pair → ShareWhy write a process in the order it happens: before sending, then after?Show the answer

Each step in time can be a mark. Going in order helps you not to miss a step.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2023, Question 4(b). Data is transmitted between a computer and a printer. An odd parity check is used to detect errors in the data transmission.

items.prompt: Explain how the odd parity check detects errors.
items.modelAnswer: A parity bit is added to each byte before transmission, to make the number of 1s odd. After transmission the 1s are counted. If the number is even, an error is detected.
scheme: the number of 1s / 0s are counted
a parity bit is added to each byte / 7 bits before transmission
... to make the sum of the bits / 1s or 0s in each byte odd
after transmission, if the number is odd no error is detected
after transmission, if the number is even an error is detected
items.context: Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2023, Question 4(b). Data is transmitted between a computer and a printer. An odd parity check is used to detect errors in the data transmission. Marking rule: Any four from, one mark for each point met, up to 4.

steps.label: Error Detection: The Checksum
steps.content:
Error Detection: The Checksum

Think → Pair → ShareA checksum and a check digit both calculate a value. Why do they find errors at different times?Show the answer

A check digit checks data when it is entered. A checksum checks data after it is transmitted.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2025, Question 4(b)(i). A restaurant's ordering system transmits each customer's order across its network to a computer in the kitchen. A checksum is used to check the data for errors after transmission.

items.prompt: Describe the process of the checksum error detection method.
items.modelAnswer: The checksum is calculated from the data, using an algorithm. It is transmitted with the data. The receiver recalculates it. If the two values do not match, an error is detected.
scheme: the checksum is calculated from / using the data
... using an algorithm // by example
the (checksum) value is transmitted with the data
the (checksum) value is recalculated after transmission / by the recipient
if the checksum values do not match, an error is detected // if the checksum values match, no error is detected ...
... request for the data to be resent if there is an error
items.context: Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2025, Question 4(b)(i). A restaurant's ordering system transmits each customer's order across its network to a computer in the kitchen. A checksum is used to check the data for errors after transmission. Marking rule: Any five from, one mark for each point met, up to 5.

steps.label: Activity 1: Be the Sender, Be the Receiver
steps.content:
Activity 1: Be the Sender, Be the Receiver

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must the receiver check the data before it sends anything back?Show the answer

What it sends back depends on whether the data arrived safely, so it must find that out first.

Be the receiver: check each byte and decide what to send back. Be the sender: decide which packet to send next. New bytes every time. Stuck? Switch on I need help.

steps.label: Error Detection: Parity Checks and ARQ
steps.content:
Error Detection: Parity Checks and ARQ

Think → Pair → ShareThis answer is about two methods. Why plan which marks come from each one?Show the answer

The mark scheme gives at most four marks for ARQ, so you need points about parity too. A plan stops you writing about only one method.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2022, Question 9. A system uses parity checks and automatic repeat queries (ARQ) to detect and correct errors in the transmission of data.

items.prompt: Describe how parity checks and ARQ operate together to detect and correct errors.
items.modelAnswer: Even parity is agreed. A parity bit is added to each byte to make the number of 1s even. When the data is sent, a timer is started. If no error is found, a positive acknowledgement is sent. If no acknowledgement arrives before the timeout, the data is resent.
scheme: odd or even parity is set / agreed for the data
a parity bit is added to each byte of data
... to make the number of 1s match the parity
data is checked after transmission to see if the parity is correct
ARQ uses acknowledgement and timeout
if no error is found, a positive acknowledgement is sent to the sender / no acknowledgement is sent to the sender
if an error is found, a negative acknowledgement is sent to the sender ...
... that triggers the data to be resent
when the data is sent, a timer is started
if an acknowledgement is not received within the time set, the data is resent ...
... until an acknowledgement is received / the resend limit is reached
items.context: Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2022, Question 9. A system uses parity checks and automatic repeat queries (ARQ) to detect and correct errors in the transmission of data. Marking rule: Any six from (MAX four for ARQ), one mark for each point met, up to 6.

steps.label: Error Detection: Fix the Answer
steps.content:
Error Detection: Fix the Answer

Think → Pair → ShareWhy check a student answer one sentence at a time?Show the answer

One sentence can be right and the next one wrong. That shows where the marks are lost.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2024, Question 2(f)(i). Explain how the echo check is used to check for errors in the email data.

items.prompt:
A student wrote: “The employer's device sends the data back and checks it. If the copies are the same, there is an error.”
This answer gets 1 mark. Write a better answer that gets 3 marks.
items.modelAnswer: A copy is sent back to the sender. The sender compares it with the data sent. If they do not match, there is an error.
scheme: a copy of the data is sent back to the employee's device / the sender
the employee's device / the sender compares the data sent to the data received back
if the original and the copy do not match, an error has occurred
items.ariaLabel: Explain how the echo check is used to check for errors in the email data. (better answer)
items.context: Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2024, Question 2(f)(i). Explain how the echo check is used to check for errors in the email data. A student wrote: "The employer's device sends the data back and checks it. If the copies are the same, there is an error." This got 1 of 3 marks: the sender compares, not the receiver, and an error is when the copies do NOT match. The student now writes a better answer. Marking rule: One mark each, one mark for each point met, up to 3.

steps.label: Error Detection: Which Method?
steps.content:
Error Detection: Which Method?

Think → Pair → ShareWhy test each statement against every method?Show the answer

Some statements fit more than one method. Testing each one stops you missing one.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2021, Question 3(a). For each statement, type the method or methods it applies to: checksum, check digit or parity check. Some apply to more than one.

Total: 5 marks

steps.label: Encryption: Symmetric Encryption
steps.content:
Encryption: Symmetric Encryption

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can "the data is scrambled" on its own not get full marks here?Show the answer

It is true, but it is one general idea. Each mark needs a different, exact fact that uses the right terms.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2022, Question 4(b)(ii). Rebekah decides to encrypt the data that she transmits whilst using the Internet. She does this to keep the data safe. The data is encrypted using symmetric encryption.

items.prompt: Describe how the data is encrypted using symmetric encryption.
items.modelAnswer: The data is encrypted and decrypted using the same key. Plain text is encrypted into cipher text. The key is sent to the receiver.
scheme: data is encrypted and decrypted using the same key / algorithm
data before encryption is known as plain text
data after encryption is known as cypher text
the key is sent to the receiver (to allow the data to be decrypted) // values are sent to the receiver that are used to generate the key
items.context: Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2022, Question 4(b)(ii). Rebekah decides to encrypt the data that she transmits whilst using the Internet. She does this to keep the data safe. The data is encrypted using symmetric encryption. Marking rule: One from the first point, then any three from the rest, one mark for each point met, up to 4.

steps.label: Encryption: Fix the Answer
steps.content:
Encryption: Fix the Answer

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does the word "whereas" help in a difference answer?Show the answer

It joins what one method does to what the other does instead, so the examiner sees the contrast.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2024, Question 2(g)(iii). Give two differences between symmetric encryption and asymmetric encryption.

items.prompt:
A student wrote: “Symmetric encryption is more secure. Asymmetric encryption scrambles the data.”
This answer gets 0 marks. Write a better answer that gets 2 marks.
items.modelAnswer: Symmetric uses one key, whereas asymmetric uses two keys. Symmetric decrypts with the same key, whereas asymmetric decrypts with a different key.
scheme: symmetric uses one / public key whereas asymmetric uses two / public and private keys
symmetric can send the key with the data whereas asymmetric does not
symmetric decrypts the data using the same key whereas asymmetric decrypts the data using a different key
symmetric is less secure than asymmetric
items.ariaLabel: Give two differences between symmetric encryption and asymmetric encryption. (better answer)
items.context: Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2024, Question 2(g)(iii). Give two differences between symmetric encryption and asymmetric encryption. A student wrote: "Symmetric encryption is more secure. Asymmetric encryption scrambles the data." This got 0 of 2 marks: symmetric is less secure, and both methods scramble the data, so that is not a difference. The student now writes a better answer. Marking rule: Any two from, one mark for each point met, up to 2.
